question.question: At equal parameters (within 5%), equal exposure and the same recipe, does a pure 2D GPS++-style message-passing network (atom, bond and molecule states, direct bond-molecule paths, in-model RWSE16, no attention) beat BondLocal+PairNorm GPTrans-T on matched 100K development MAE?
question.deficiency: GPTrans-T pays for dense pair tensors and attention; K1 and GPS-style adapters on top of it gave no gain, so it is open whether global attention is needed for this target at 100K.
alternatives: Attention and the dense pair state are necessary at 100K
A 100K effect is not stable or does not survive 500K (earlier gains shrank to 0.21-0.37x)
Any gain comes from in-model RWSE16 instead of the backbone
question.positive_decision: Nominate only per the frozen bands in protocol.md (effect <= -4.6 meV, paired CI upper < 0); no automatic scale-up.
question.negative_decision: Close this GPS++ MPNN backbone at 100K without hyperparameter grids, retries, ablation or 500K.

profile.cheapest_falsifier: One same-job 100K 60-pass T4x2 pair: BondLocal+PairNorm GPTrans-T (control, from gptrans.pt) against the GPS++ MPNN, same recipe.
